title: Smallest Value of the Rearranged Number
summary: Given an integer, rearrange its digits to form the smallest possible number without leading zeros, maintaining the original sign.
statement: Given an integer, rearrange its digits to form the smallest possible number without leading zeros, maintaining the original sign.
constraints: Use exactly the decimal digits of abs(num), preserving the original sign.
A positive result may not begin with zero; zero itself returns zero.
For a negative input, minimizing the signed value means maximizing its absolute digit arrangement.
hints: The sign changes which digit ordering is optimal.
Use descending digits for negatives; for positives sort ascending but swap the first nonzero digit into the leading position.
Handle zero, branch by sign, arrange digits, and convert back to an integer.
Descending maximizes magnitude for a negative result. For positives, the smallest nonzero leading digit followed by all remaining digits ascending is lexicographically and numerically minimal.
editorial: Descending maximizes magnitude for a negative result. For positives, the smallest nonzero leading digit followed by all remaining digits ascending is lexicographically and numerically minimal.

tests.explanation: The ascending digits are 0,1,3; move the first nonzero digit forward to obtain 103.
Descending absolute digits form 7650, so the smallest signed result is -7650.
